title.narrative: North Kordofan Food Security and Livelihood Recovery Project

description.narrative:
According to the 2008 census, the North Kordofan state has a population of approximately 3.2 million, of which approximately 85% is rural.This State is particularly unique because it has high economic potential and is politically stable. It is considered a safe haven relative to its’ neighbouring warring states of South Kordfan as well as North, East and South Darfur. But the ongoing conflict in South Kordofan has resulted in an increased number of internally displaced persons (IDPs) seeking refuge in North Kordofan for safety reasons and to access livelihood opportunities and basic services. Since the drought and famine in the 1980’s, the state has also witnessed an influx of rural communities from North Kordofan fleeing into the peripheries of major urban centres, specifically El Obeid. The majority of IDPs are settled in Sheikan locality. The IDP families are either from a farming or pastoralist background or have skills in small scale business. This project therefore plans to tap on the livelihood improvement potential around crop farming and pastoralist for improved food security and livelihood. – as per vulnerable target livelihood background. Problem Analysis As result of the displacements factors mentioned above, the selected families are unable to secure their livelihoods due to:· disruption in traditional livelihood patterns asset loss
disruption of social services
Project Objective: To provide food security and livelihood recovery for displaced and vulnerable women, men and their families in the Sheikan locality.This Intervention will target: 21 villages (11 villages are dependant on small scale farming and 10 villages on livestock rearing)2,000 men, women and their families that are dependant on small scale farming and livestock rearing. 12,000 individuals[1](8,000 men and 4,000 women) will be reached indirectly. Another estimated 400 households will be reached via access to community-based animal health expertise provided by CAHWs. [1] Average family size is 6 individuals per household
